speaker_role: essay editor at an editing company (Kevin, Wordvice)
commercial_incentive: Wordvice sells essay editing and proofreading; the video ends with a promotion and recommends professional editing.
key_insights: Admissions readers are framed as asking whether you can write and whether you fit the school.
Reflect on an experience rather than narrate it, and tie lessons to what college will demand.
Do not spend multiple paragraphs on the personal story; connect it to academic growth and consider returning to it at the end.
Do not list awards, scores, or grades that appear elsewhere; avoid repeating the same details.
Suggests having an editor review the essay, which is self-serving given the channel.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Wordvice says it received over 5,000 college application essays during the 2020 season.
notable_or_distinctive: Mostly generic advice; the bookending suggestion is the slight extra.
reliability_notes: Sales framing, and the claim that admissions officers often recommend professional editing is unsupported (and conflicts with other speakers here).
